items.detail: Must be valid at least six months past 16 Oct. Currently with the Chinese consulate in Atlanta for the visa.
In process. Confirm with info@chinaatlanta.org.
No permit, no boarding for Lhasa. Normally handed over at the last hotel before Tibet, so most likely The Westin Xi'an.
Use the Dossier export from this page. Phones die and Chinese stations often want paper.
Talk to a doctor about acetazolamide. Lhasa is 3,656 m and the train crosses Tanggula Pass at 5,072 m.
Hydration is the cheapest altitude insurance.
UV on the plateau is brutal even when the air is cold.
Dark lenses - glacier-grade if you have them.
Lhasa in October runs roughly 18C by day and freezing at night.
Two sets - one to wear, one dry.
Standard practice in a soft sleeper.
Install and verify it works before leaving. Setting one up from inside China is much harder.
Link a foreign card and test a payment. Cash and foreign cards are near-useless with small vendors.
A Hong Kong or international eSIM routes around the firewall on data.
Under 100 Wh to stay airline-legal. The train legs are long and outlets are shared.
China runs 220V; sockets take both flat A and angled I pins.
For temple donations, small stalls and anywhere the apps fail.
Every Chinese train car has a boiling-water dispenser. This is how you eat well on a 34-hour ride.
Instant noodles, nuts, fruit. The dining car is fine but limited.
Soft sleeper is a four-berth compartment with strangers.
Public restrooms rarely supply either.
Sandra got sick in Xi'an - possibly from the water. Worth the caution.
